answer: Pay graders with correlated-agreement scoring, a peer-prediction rule. A grader earns for matching a random peer on the same answer, minus how often they match a peer on a different, unrelated answer. A sybil ring that rates everything high matches everywhere, so the penalty cancels the bonus and it earns nothing; only graders who actually tell answers apart get paid. A gale of identical votes can't lift a weak answer to the summit, and by dawn of the next epoch the ring's grading income is zero. Limit: each answer needs enough honest graders to compare against.
